result:
A race condition is when the result depends on the unpredictable timing of two or more processes touching the same resource. With a shared log, that means lines from different writers interleaving or cutting each other in half.

To avoid it, take an exclusive lock around the append with `flock`:

```sh
{
  flock 9
  echo "$(date -Is) $$ started job"
  echo "$(date -Is) $$ details: $details"
} 9>>/var/log/stockroom.log.lock >>/var/log/stockroom.log
```

The lock is released when the block ends and file descriptor 9 closes, even if the script dies. Every writer has to use the same lock file for it to work.

A single short `echo ... >> file` is already safe on a local filesystem, because `>>` opens the file in append mode and each small write lands whole at the end. You need the lock when one entry spans several writes, when lines are long (several KB or more), or when the log is on NFS; note that `flock` itself can be unreliable on NFS.
